event.e1_1.title: Festival sale
event.e1_1.intro: It is festival season and everything is on sale. A phone cover with earbuds is ₹1,500 as a combo. The cover alone is ₹600. You only planned to buy a cover.
event.e1_1.combo.label: Buy the combo for ₹1,500
event.e1_1.combo.outcome: You paid ₹1,500. The earbuds are fun, and nothing went toward your goal this month.
event.e1_1.combo.why: A sale only saves money on things you already planned to buy.
event.e1_1.cover.label: Buy only the cover for ₹600
event.e1_1.cover.outcome: You paid ₹600 for the thing you had planned.
event.e1_1.cover.why: A small want, planned, fits inside your month.
event.e1_1.skip.label: Skip the sale and put ₹600 toward your goal
event.e1_1.skip.why: Wants can wait. Goals move when you feed them.
event.e1_2.title: A friend's birthday
event.e1_2.intro: Your friend's birthday is this week. The group is collecting ₹500 each for a party.
event.e1_2.contribute.label: Put in ₹500
event.e1_2.contribute.outcome: You paid ₹500 and had a great evening.
event.e1_2.contribute.why: Spending on friends is a real want. It still needs room in your plan.
event.e1_2.handmade.label: Make a gift for ₹150
event.e1_2.handmade.outcome: You spent ₹150 on a gift you made yourself. Your friend loved it.
event.e1_2.handmade.why: You can show up for people inside your own limit.
event.e1_2.skip.label: Skip the party
event.e1_2.skip.outcome: You kept your money and missed the evening.
event.e1_2.skip.why: Saying no saves money, and it has a cost too.
event.e1_3.title: A surprise ₹1,500
event.e1_3.intro: A relative hands you ₹1,500 as a surprise gift.
event.e1_3.spend.label: Spend all of it
event.e1_3.spend.outcome: The ₹1,500 came and went in the same week. Fun, and nothing saved.
event.e1_3.spend.why: When spending comes first, saving often never happens.
event.e1_3.split.label: Enjoy ₹900 and save ₹600
event.e1_3.split.outcome: You enjoyed ₹900 and put ₹600 toward your goal.
event.e1_3.split.why: Pay yourself first: set aside a share before you spend.
event.e1_3.save.label: Save all ₹1,500
event.e1_3.save.why: Saving it all is healthy. A little joy belongs in a good plan too.
event.e2_1.title: ₹3,000 in cash
event.e2_1.intro: You are given ₹3,000 in cash. Where does it go?
event.e2_1.drawer.label: Keep it in a drawer at home
event.e2_1.drawer.outcome: The ₹3,000 is in your drawer, easy to reach.
event.e2_1.drawer.why: Cash at hand gets spent, and it can be lost.
event.e2_1.drawer.later: ₹800 of the cash in your drawer went on small spends you cannot remember.
event.e2_1.bank.label: Put it in your savings account
event.e2_1.bank.outcome: The ₹3,000 is in your savings account. It earns a little every month.
event.e2_1.bank.why: A bank account is safe, earns a little and leaves a record.
event.e2_1.spend.label: Spend it on something you want
event.e2_1.spend.outcome: You spent the ₹3,000 on something you wanted.
event.e2_1.spend.why: Fun today. Money that is spent cannot grow.
event.e2_2.title: "Refund waiting"
event.e2_2.intro: A message arrives: "Refund of ₹500 is waiting. Enter your UPI PIN to receive it."
event.e2_2.pin.label: Enter the PIN
event.e2_2.pin.outcome: ₹1,500 left your account. There was no refund.
event.e2_2.pin.why: A UPI PIN is only for sending money. You never enter it to receive.
event.e2_2.ignore.label: Ignore the message
event.e2_2.ignore.outcome: You did not reply. Nothing happened to your money.
event.e2_2.ignore.why: An unexpected "refund" message can simply be left alone.
event.e2_2.ask.label: Ask an adult and call the bank
event.e2_2.ask.outcome: You asked an adult and called the bank on its official number. It was a scam.
event.e2_2.ask.why: Pause and check with someone you trust before you tap.
event.e2_3.title: Two accounts
event.e2_3.intro: You can keep your savings in one of two accounts. Account A: no minimum balance, 2.5% interest a year. Account B: 3.5% interest a year, but if your balance is under ₹5,000 you pay ₹150 every three months.
event.e2_3.b.label: Choose Account B
event.e2_3.b.outcome: You picked the higher interest. While your balance is under ₹5,000, ₹150 comes out every three months.
event.e2_3.b.why: Read the fee line. A fee can be bigger than the extra interest.
event.e2_3.a.label: Choose Account A
event.e2_3.a.outcome: No minimum and no fee. The interest is a little lower.
event.e2_3.a.why: On a small balance, having no fee can matter more than a higher rate.
event.e2_3.read.label: Read the full terms, then choose
event.e2_3.read.outcome: The terms showed the ₹150 fee clearly. With your balance, you went with Account A.
event.e2_3.read.why: Two minutes with the terms showed the real cost.
event.e3_1.title: Your phone screen breaks
event.e3_1.intro: Your phone slips and the screen cracks. The repair costs ₹2,800.
event.e3_1.fund.label: Pay from your emergency fund
event.e3_1.fund.outcome: The repair came out of your emergency fund. Your goals did not move.
event.e3_1.fund.why: This is exactly what an emergency fund is for.
event.e3_1.goal.label: Take it from your goal money
event.e3_1.goal.outcome: You paid from the money set aside for your goal. The goal moves back a month.
event.e3_1.goal.why: It works, but your goal has to wait.
event.e3_1.lender.label: Borrow from a moneylender
event.e3_1.lender.outcome: A moneylender gave you ₹2,800 at 10% a month. You pay ₹280 every month, and the ₹2,800 is still owed at the end of three months.
event.e3_1.lender.why: Borrowing with no paperwork can cost the most.
event.e3_1.skip.label: Leave it cracked
event.e3_1.skip.outcome: You kept your money and now use a cracked screen.
event.e3_1.skip.why: You avoided the cost and lost some use.
event.e3_2.title: A week of illness
event.e3_2.intro: You fall ill. Tests and medicine come to ₹3,500.
event.e3_2.insured.label: Use your health insurance
event.e3_2.insured.outcome: Your health insurance paid most of the bill. You paid ₹500.
event.e3_2.insured.why: Insurance took the big part of the cost.
event.e3_2.fund.label: Pay from your emergency fund
event.e3_2.fund.why: The fund did its job. Now it needs refilling.
event.e3_2.goal.label: Take it from your goal money
event.e3_2.goal.outcome: You paid ₹3,500 from the money set aside for your goal.
event.e3_2.goal.why: With no safety net, a shock lands on your goals.
event.e3_2.lender.label: Borrow from a moneylender
event.e3_2.lender.outcome: A moneylender gave you ₹3,500 at 10% a month. You pay ₹350 every month, and the ₹3,500 is still owed at the end of three months.
event.e3_2.lender.why: A shock without a safety net often ends in costly borrowing.
event.e3_3.title: Instalment or impulse?
event.e3_3.intro: A ₹500 saving instalment is due this week. The same week, something you want shows up for ₹500.
event.e3_3.rd.label: Pay the instalment, skip the want
event.e3_3.rd.outcome: Your instalment goes in as planned. The want can wait a month.
event.e3_3.skip.label: Buy the want, skip the instalment
event.e3_3.skip.outcome: You spent ₹500 on the want. The bank charged ₹50 for the missed instalment.
event.e3_3.skip.why: Missing a deposit costs a fee and slows the habit.
event.e4_1.title: A phone for ₹6,000
event.e4_1.intro: A shop sells a phone for ₹6,000. Its sign says "No-cost EMI: 6 × ₹1,000". If you pay cash, the price is ₹5,500.
event.e4_1.nocost.label: Take the "no-cost" EMI
event.e4_1.nocost.outcome: You have the phone. ₹1,000 leaves your wallet every month for six months.
event.e4_1.bank.label: Take a 6-month bank loan and buy it
event.e4_1.bank.outcome: The bank lent you the money at the rate your credit score earned. You have the phone, and an EMI leaves your wallet every month for six months.
event.e4_1.bank.why: A loan's real price is the total you repay, not the monthly amount.
event.e4_1.wait.label: Wait, save and pay cash later
event.e4_1.wait.outcome: You wait and save. In a few months you can pay ₹5,500 in cash, with no interest.
event.e4_1.wait.why: The cheapest option is often patience.
event.e4_2.title: "Will you co-sign?"
event.e4_2.intro: A friend wants a ₹5,000 loan and asks you to co-sign it.
event.e4_2.cosign.label: Co-sign the loan
event.e4_2.cosign.outcome: You signed. If your friend pays on time, nothing happens to you.
event.e4_2.cosign.why: A co-signer owes the money when the borrower does not pay.
event.e4_2.cosign.later: Your friend missed a payment. The lender took ₹850 from you, and your credit score fell.
event.e4_2.decline.label: Say no, and give ₹300 of your own
event.e4_2.decline.outcome: You did not sign. You gave ₹300 to help.
event.e4_2.decline.why: You can help a friend without taking on their loan.
event.e4_3.title: An instant-loan app
event.e4_3.intro: An app offers you ₹3,000 in two minutes. It charges a ₹300 fee up front and asks for access to your contacts.
event.e4_3.accept.label: Accept the loan
event.e4_3.accept.outcome: ₹2,700 reached you after the ₹300 fee. Next month the app wants ₹3,900 back.
event.e4_3.accept.why: ₹1,200 extra on ₹2,700 in one month is about 44%.
event.e4_3.decline.label: Decline, and ask at home or at a bank
event.e4_3.decline.outcome: You closed the app and asked at home and at a bank.
event.e4_3.decline.why: Money that arrives in two minutes can be the costliest kind.
event.e4_3.check.label: Look the lender up first
event.e4_3.check.outcome: You looked for the lender on the RBI's list of lending apps. It was not there, so you declined.
event.e4_3.check.why: Check that a lender is regulated before you borrow.
event.e5_1.title: A ₹6,000 prize
event.e5_1.intro: You win a ₹6,000 prize. What do you do with it?
event.e5_1.spend.label: Spend it
event.e5_1.spend.why: No growth this time, and that is a choice too.
event.e5_1.savings.label: Put it in your savings account
event.e5_1.savings.outcome: ₹6,000 is in your savings account. You can take it out any day.
event.e5_1.savings.why: Safe and easy to reach. It grows the slowest.
event.e5_1.fd.label: Open a 6-month fixed deposit
event.e5_1.fd.outcome: ₹6,000 is in a 6-month fixed deposit. At maturity it becomes ₹6,195.
event.e5_1.fd.why: A fixed deposit pays more than a savings account, and the money is locked until it matures.
event.e5_1.split.label: Split it three ways
event.e5_1.split.outcome: ₹3,000 went into a 6-month fixed deposit, ₹2,000 into savings, and ₹1,000 on something fun.
event.e5_1.split.why: A split gives some growth, some access and a little joy.
event.e5_2.title: A class trip
event.e5_2.intro: Your class announces a trip. The ₹3,000 fee is due now.
event.e5_2.breakfd.label: Break your fixed deposit early
event.e5_2.breakfd.outcome: You broke the fixed deposit early. Your money came back with interest only at the savings rate, and you paid the fee.
event.e5_2.breakfd.why: Breaking a deposit early costs you interest.
event.e5_2.fund.label: Use your emergency fund
event.e5_2.fund.outcome: The ₹3,000 came from your emergency fund. Your deposit stayed untouched.
event.e5_2.fund.why: The fund exists for surprises like this.
event.e5_2.pay.label: Pay from your wallet
event.e5_2.pay.why: Money kept flexible is there when a date arrives.
event.e5_2.skip.label: Skip the trip
event.e5_2.skip.outcome: You kept your money and stayed back.
event.e5_2.skip.why: Saying no kept your plan intact, and it has a cost too.
event.e5_3.title: "Double your money"
event.e5_3.intro: Someone your cousin knows offers a scheme: put in ₹2,000 and it doubles in two years. "Guaranteed."
event.e5_3.invest.label: Put in ₹2,000
event.e5_3.invest.why: A promise far above normal returns means a risk you cannot see.
event.e5_3.invest.later: The "double your money" scheme has stopped answering calls. The ₹2,000 is gone.
event.e5_3.ignore.label: Ignore it
event.e5_3.ignore.why: Ignoring it kept your money. Asking why it is risky teaches you more.
event.e5_3.ask.label: Ask what the risk is and who regulates it
event.e5_3.ask.outcome: You asked what the risk is and who regulates the scheme. Nobody could answer.
event.e5_3.ask.why: A higher return always comes with a higher risk. Ask who regulates it.
event.e6_1.title: Three pretend years
event.e6_1.intro: Imagine ₹6,000 over three pretend years. Pick a mix to see how it would have behaved. This is a preview: nothing in your portfolio changes.
event.e6_1.shares.label: All in shares
event.e6_1.shares.outcome: In the pretend years, all-in-shares moved the most, up and down.
event.e6_1.shares.why: One kind of asset means every swing reaches all of your money.
event.e6_1.mix.label: A mix of deposit, gold and mutual fund
event.e6_1.mix.outcome: In the pretend years, the mix moved less than shares alone.
event.e6_1.mix.why: When one part falls, another part may hold steady. That is diversification.
event.e6_1.savings.label: All in savings
event.e6_1.savings.outcome: In the pretend years, all-in-savings barely moved, and it grew the least.
event.e6_1.savings.why: Low risk and low return usually travel together.
event.e6_2.title: ₹3,000 into gold?
event.e6_2.intro: You are thinking of putting ₹3,000 into gold. There is more than one way to do it.
event.e6_2.jewellery.label: Buy a gold coin from a jeweller
event.e6_2.jewellery.outcome: ₹3,000 bought gold worth ₹2,760. The 8% making charge was gone on day one.
event.e6_2.jewellery.why: Making charges come off the value straight away.
event.e6_2.etf.label: Buy regulated paper gold
event.e6_2.etf.outcome: ₹3,000 bought regulated paper gold worth ₹2,985, after a 0.5% cost.
event.e6_2.etf.why: A lower cost leaves more of your money in gold.
event.e6_2.app.label: Buy through a "digital gold" app advert
event.e6_2.app.outcome: You could not find out who regulates the app, or where the gold is kept.
event.e6_2.app.why: If you cannot tell who regulates a product, find out before any money moves.
event.e6_2.none.label: Not now
event.e6_2.none.outcome: You kept your ₹3,000 where it was.
event.e6_2.none.why: Not buying is a choice too. Gold pays no interest while you hold it.
event.e6_3.title: The market turns
event.e6_3.intro: The news is full of falling prices. Your mutual fund will show it over the next two months.
event.e6_3.watch.label: Check prices every day
event.e6_3.watch.outcome: You start checking prices every day. Each small fall feels bigger than it is.
event.e6_3.watch.why: Watching every move makes a fall feel worse.
event.e6_3.plan.label: Stick to your monthly check
event.e6_3.plan.outcome: You decide to look once a month, when you plan your money.
event.e6_3.plan.why: A fixed time to review keeps mood out of money decisions.
event.e6_4.title: A stock tip
event.e6_4.intro: A message in a group chat says one company's stock "will double in a month". Many people reply that they are buying.
event.e6_4.buy.label: Put ₹2,000 into the tipped stock
event.e6_4.buy.outcome: You put ₹2,000 into the tipped stock.
event.e6_4.buy.why: A tip is not research. Whoever sent it may profit when you buy.
event.e6_4.buy.later: The tipped stock jumped, then crashed. Your ₹2,000 is now worth about ₹1,380.
event.e6_4.ignore.label: Ignore it
event.e6_4.ignore.why: Ignoring a tip protects your money. Checking who sent it teaches you why.
event.e6_4.check.label: Check who sent it
event.e6_4.check.outcome: You checked. The sender is not registered to give investment advice.
event.e6_4.check.why: Before you listen to advice, check that the adviser is registered.
event.e6_5.title: Your fund is down 19%
event.e6_5.intro: Two months of falling prices. Your mutual fund is about 19% lower than before the fall.
event.e6_5.sell.label: Sell everything
event.e6_5.sell.outcome: You sold at the low price. The fall is now a real loss.
event.e6_5.sell.why: Selling in a panic turns a dip into a loss.
event.e6_5.hold.label: Hold, and keep the SIP going
event.e6_5.hold.outcome: You held on and kept your SIP running. It buys more units while prices are low.
event.e6_5.hold.why: A fixed monthly amount buys more units when prices fall. That is rupee-cost averaging.
event.e6_5.pause.label: Hold, but pause the SIP
event.e6_5.pause.outcome: You kept what you hold and paused the SIP.
event.e6_5.pause.why: You avoided selling low, and missed buying at lower prices.
event.e7_1.title: Your first stipend
event.e7_1.intro: Your first ₹8,000 stipend arrives with a pay slip. The slip lists what was taken out before the money reached you.
event.e7_1.read.label: Read the slip and keep it
event.e7_1.read.outcome: You read every line and saved the slip.
event.e7_1.read.why: Know where your money goes before it reaches you.
event.e7_1.ignore.label: Ignore the slip
event.e7_1.ignore.outcome: The money arrived. You do not know what was taken out, or why.
event.e7_1.ignore.why: A pay slip is the record of your own income.
event.e7_2.title: A weekend job paid in cash
event.e7_2.intro: You earn ₹2,500 a month in cash from a weekend job.
event.e7_2.record.label: Write it down every month
event.e7_2.record.outcome: You note the date and amount every month.
event.e7_2.record.why: A record of income helps later with loans and forms.
event.e7_2.skip.label: Don't bother recording it
event.e7_2.skip.outcome: The cash comes and goes with no record.
event.e7_2.skip.why: Income with no record is hard to prove when you need to.
event.e8_1.title: A "task job"
event.e8_1.intro: An online "job" pays ₹50 for each small task. After a few payments it says: "Deposit ₹2,000 to unlock ₹5,000."
event.e8_1.deposit.label: Deposit the ₹2,000
event.e8_1.deposit.outcome: You sent ₹2,000. Now they ask for more to "unlock" it.
event.e8_1.deposit.why: Small early payouts build false trust before the big ask.
event.e8_1.report.label: Stop and report it
event.e8_1.report.outcome: You stopped, called 1930 and reported it on cybercrime.gov.in.
event.e8_1.report.why: Reporting fast gives the strongest chance of stopping the money.
event.e8_1.check.label: Run the 5-point check with an adult
event.e8_1.check.outcome: You ran the five checks with an adult. It failed on the first one.
event.e8_1.check.why: A real job never asks you to pay to get paid.
event.e8_2.title: "Your KYC expires today"
event.e8_2.intro: An SMS says your KYC expires today and gives a link to "update" it.
event.e8_2.click.label: Open the link and enter your details
event.e8_2.click.outcome: You entered your details on a fake page. ₹1,500 left your account.
event.e8_2.click.why: Banks do not ask for your details through a link in a message.
event.e8_2.delete.label: Delete and report the message
event.e8_2.delete.outcome: You deleted the message and reported it.
event.e8_2.delete.why: A message that rushes you is a reason to slow down.
event.e8_2.call.label: Call the bank's official number
event.e8_2.call.outcome: You called the number printed on your passbook. Your KYC was fine.
event.e8_2.call.why: Use the number you already have, never the one in the message.
event.e8_3.title: A tips group
event.e8_3.intro: A group promises to turn ₹2,000 into ₹20,000 in a week. "Join now, limited seats."
event.e8_3.join.label: Join and pay ₹2,000
event.e8_3.join.outcome: You paid ₹2,000. The group went silent.
event.e8_3.ignore.label: Ignore it
event.e8_3.ignore.why: Ignoring it kept your money. Checking it teaches you the signs.
event.e8_3.check.label: Check whether they are registered
event.e8_3.check.outcome: You checked whether they are registered to advise on investments. They are not.
event.e8_3.check.why: Anyone who handles other people's investments must be registered.
